title: Define a projection capability and budget ladder

state.decision_rationale: Accepted as named profiles, exact/numbered/signatures/outline/reference/alias projections, and explicit loss posture.

provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Document a tier ladder such as index-only to symbols to signatures to exact, with a byte or token budget target. That would make the format a default for context engineering.
feedback.normalized_claim: Define named, capability-explicit packet profiles and projection tiers that trade exactness for navigation and enforce a declared context budget.

current_behavior: File records declare projection=exact, numbered, or alias, while mode currently describes lossless generation.
Packets include index, global symbols, edges posture, omissions, and every selected file body by default.
There is no named capability profile for manifest-only, review, query, summarized, or budget-constrained packets.
No packet-level token estimate or budget enforcement is implemented.

proposal.summary: Unify profile, projection, and budget proposals into a capability model that makes omissions and loss posture explicit at packet and file level.
candidate_changes: Define stable named profiles and the sections, projection types, completeness claims, and verification guarantees each requires.
Declare per-file and packet byte or token estimates plus the estimator identity and version.
Specify deterministic degradation order when a caller sets a budget, including which files remain exact and why.
Keep every lossy representation linked to exact content identity or a lossless packet when available.
non_goals: Do not describe summarized or omitted content as lossless.
Do not make token counts model-independent when tokenizers differ.
Do not create overlapping profile names without a compact capability declaration consumers can check.

questions: Are profiles presets, conformance levels, or both?
Which projections are normative core capabilities versus optional extensions?
How does a budget policy rank changed files, dependencies, tests, policies, generated artifacts, and lockfiles?
risks: A tier ladder can falsely imply that more compact tiers preserve the same epistemic guarantees.
Tokenizer-specific budgets can reduce reproducibility and portability.
Too many profiles can fragment producers and consumers.
evidence_needed: Task-accuracy and token-cost benchmarks across candidate profiles.
Capability negotiation examples for consumers that support only part of the format.
Deterministic budget-selection tests and explicit omission audits.
